previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with fever, chills, and left flank pain after his percutaneous nephrostomy (PCN) tube dislodged during parasailing and was reinserted nonsterilely by his girlfriend. He was diagnosed with a PCN site infection and urinary tract infection, treated with a 5-day course of IV meropenem. His white blood cell count improved, and subsequent urine cultures showed no growth, indicating treatment success. The PCN tube was exchanged by interventional radiology, confirming proper placement and drainage. He became agitated upon discharge planning, refusing paperwork but accepting a prescription for oral fosfomycin for three doses. He declined further evaluation or treatment for his chronic left hip pressure ulcer. Follow-up was arranged with urology to discuss surgical options due to recurrent infections, and his mother was informed of the discharge plan.

INDICATION:  ___ with  abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, left sided
nephrostomy tube that fell out and was manually replaced by patient, evaluate
for intra-abdominal processes and also evaluate the position of the left
nephrostomy tube and any associated injury+PO contrast//  abdominal pain,
nausea, vomiting, left sided nephrostomy tube that fell out and was manually
replaced by patient, evaluate for intra-abdominal processes and also evaluate
the position of the left nephrostomy tube and any associated injury

TECHNIQUE:  Multidetector CT images of the abdomen and pelvis were acquired
without intravenous contrast. Non-contrast scan has several limitations in
detecting vascular and parenchymal organ abnormalities, including tumor
detection.
Oral contrast was not administered.
Coronal and sagittal reformations were performed and reviewed on PACS.

DOSE:  Acquisition sequence:
   1) Spiral Acquisition 4.5 s, 48.9 cm; CTDIvol = 9.4 mGy (Body) DLP = 457.6
mGy-cm.
 Total DLP (Body) = 458 mGy-cm.

COMPARISON:  CT abdomen pelvis from ___.

FINDINGS: 

LOWER CHEST: Visualized lung fields are within normal limits besides bibasilar
atelectasis, worse on the left.  There is no evidence of pleural or
pericardial effusion.

ABDOMEN: Examination is limited secondary to lack of intravenous contrast and
artifact from posterior fixation hardware.

HEPATOBILIARY: The liver demonstrates homogeneous attenuation throughout. 
There is no evidence of focal lesions within the limitations of an unenhanced
scan.  There is no evidence of intrahepatic or extrahepatic biliary
dilatation.  The gallbladder is within normal limits.

PANCREAS: The pancreas has normal attenuation throughout, without evidence of
focal lesions within the limitations of an unenhanced scan.  There is no
pancreatic ductal dilatation.  There is no peripancreatic stranding.

SPLEEN: The spleen shows normal size and attenuation throughout, without
evidence of focal lesions.

ADRENALS: The right and left adrenal glands are normal in size and shape.

URINARY: Right kidney appears relatively atrophic.  Prominence of an
extrarenal pelvis is noted.  Cannot clearly delineate hydronephrosis on this
limited exam.  Left kidney contains a percutaneous nephrostomy tube which is
appropriately positioned.  No obvious hydronephrosis based on limitations
detailed above.  Left perinephric stranding is similar compared to prior.  No
visualized nephrolithiasis.

GASTROINTESTINAL: There is a small to moderate hiatal hernia.  Stomach is
otherwise notable for relative distension with intraluminal contents.  Small
bowel is grossly within normal limits.  Anastomotic site is noted in the right
lower quadrant.  Moderate stool seen within the colon.  The appendix is not
clearly delineated.

PELVIS: Native bladder is decompressed.  Ileal conduit is not clearly
delineated but ostomy site noted in the right lower quadrant.  There is no
free fluid in the pelvis.

REPRODUCTIVE ORGANS: The visualized reproductive organs are unremarkable.

LYMPH NODES: There is no retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymphadenopathy.  There
is no pelvic or inguinal lymphadenopathy.

VASCULAR: There is no abdominal aortic aneurysm.  Mild atherosclerotic disease
is noted.

BONES: Chronic T12 compression deformity is again noted.  Posterior fixation
hardware at the lower thoracic and upper lumbar spine is seen without
complication.  Chronic right femoral fracture with nonunion and heterotopic
ossification is partially visualized.  Left hip chronic posterior dislocation
with secondary deformity of the acetabulum is unchanged.  No acute fracture or
suspicious osseous lesion.

SOFT TISSUES: The abdominal and pelvic wall is otherwise within normal limits.

IMPRESSION: 

No change since prior.  Left percutaneous nephrostomy tube is in appropriate
position.
Other details as above noting limited visualization of abdominal structures
due to significant artifact and lack of intravenous contrast.

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with paraplegia, neurogenic bladder s/p ileostomy
c/b left ureteral stricture. Patient maintained with Left sided PCN which fell
out and patient self replaced.// Assess, exchange left sided PCN

COMPARISON:  ___ CT abdomen pelvis.

TECHNIQUE:  OPERATORS: Dr. ___ and
Dr. ___ radiologist performed the procedure. Dr. ___
___ supervised the trainee during the key components of the procedure
and has reviewed and agrees with the trainee's findings.
ANESTHESIA: Moderate sedation was provided by administrating divided doses of
25mcg of fentanyl and 0.5 mg of midazolam throughout the total intra-service
time of 5 minutes during which the patient's hemodynamic parameters were
continuously monitored by an independent trained radiology nurse. 1% lidocaine
was injected in the skin and subcutaneous tissues overlying the access site.
MEDICATIONS: The patient is currently receiving IV meropenem.
CONTRAST: 15 ml of Optiray contrast.
FLUOROSCOPY TIME AND DOSE:  1.2 min, 1 mGy

PROCEDURE:
1. Left diagnostic antegrade nephrostogram.
2. Left 8 ___ nephrostomy exchange.

PROCEDURE DETAILS: Following the discussion of the risks, benefits and
alternatives to the procedure, written informed consent was obtained from the
patient.The patient was then brought to the angiography suite and placed prone
on the exam table. A pre-procedure time-out was performed per ___ protocol. 
The left flank was prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion.

Diluted contrast was injected into the left nephrostomy to confirm catheter
position. The image was stored on PACS. Local anesthesia was administered with
instillation of lidocaine jelly and 1% subcutaneous lidocaine injection. The
catheter was cut.  A ___ wire was advanced into the left nephrostomy tube
and advanced into the distal ureter. The stay sutures were cut and the
catheter was removed over the wire. A new 8 ___ nephrostomy catheter was
flushed and advanced with its plastic stiffener over the wire into appropriate
position. The wire and stiffener were removed and the pigtail was formed.
Contrast injection confirmed appropriate positioning. The final image was
saved. The catheter was then flushed, stay sutures applied and the catheter
was secured with a Stat Lock device and sterile dressings.  The catheter was
attached to a bag for drainage.

The patient tolerated the procedure well and there were no immediate
post-procedure complications.

FINDINGS:


1. Left antegrade nephrostogram shows contrast flowing throughout the ureter
to the conduit.
2. Appropriate final position of left nephrostomy tube.

IMPRESSION: 

Technically successful left 8 ___ nephrostomy exchange.
